name: Gliclazide
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Gliclazide is cleared by the liver to inactive metabolites (under 1% leaves unchanged in urine), but hypoglycemia is more likely and can be prolonged in kidney impairment. Irish SmPCs keep the usual regimen with careful monitoring in mild to moderate impairment and contraindicate it in severe renal insufficiency, where insulin is recommended. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The SmPCs grade renal impairment as mild, moderate or severe without numeric thresholds; our bands map 'severe' to creatinine clearance (CrCl) below 30 mL/min.

bands.recommendation: Usual dosing. Modified-release (MR): 30 to 120 mg once daily at breakfast. Immediate-release 80 mg tablets: 40 to 80 mg/day to start, maximum 320 mg/day; doses above 160 mg/day are split before breakfast and dinner (SmPC).

Mild to moderate impairment: same regimen as normal kidney function with careful glucose monitoring (MR SmPC). Immediate-release: use caution above 160 mg/day and consider limiting the maximum dose as serum creatinine rises (IR SmPC). Start at the lowest dose (MR 30 mg or IR 40–80 mg) and titrate slowly; reduce if hypoglycemia occurs (KDIGO 2022, Figure 6).

Severe renal insufficiency: contraindicated; insulin is recommended (SmPC). Our mapping of 'severe' to CrCl <30 is a judgment. Off-label use below 30 is a specialist decision: lowest dose, close glucose monitoring.

hd.text: Contraindicated (severe renal insufficiency; SmPC). Dialysis does not remove gliclazide because it is highly protein-bound (SmPC 4.9).

crrt.text: Not appropriate; contraindicated in severe renal insufficiency (SmPC). Use insulin.

dialyzable: No: dialysis is of no benefit in overdose because gliclazide is about 95% protein-bound (SmPC 4.9).
monitoring: Glucose (fasting plasma glucose, glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c], self-monitoring). Hypoglycemia can be prolonged in severe kidney impairment and needs longer observation (SmPC 4.4). Reassess kidney function periodically. G6PD deficiency: sulfonylureas can cause hemolytic anemia; use with caution and consider a non-sulfonylurea alternative (SmPC 4.4).

pediatric.approved_ages: Not established in children and adolescents (SmPC).

renal.recommendation: Not established in children; kidney dosing not applicable.

adult: SmPCs give no CrCl/eGFR cut-offs; mapping 'severe renal insufficiency' to CrCl <30 is our judgment (Dr. Rivero to confirm).

Older Irish IR SmPC (2020) used for the 80 mg immediate-release dose because most PH products are 80 mg IR; PH package insert (e.g., Diamicron DR-X626) is a scanned PDF with no text layer and could not be read.
Our CrCl 30–59 band is green (usual dose with monitoring), following the colchicine convention.

revision_log.change: CrCl 30–59: lowest starting dose, slow titration (KDIGO 2022); tile kept green (label-consistent).
Red kept at CrCl <30, HD, PD, CRRT; off-label use below 30 is a specialist decision.
